summary: Apache-Sitgreaves lookout at 8,538 ft: a 1933 Aermotor tower on a site used since 1928; NRHP-listed 1988, NHLR-registered 2002, reported in active service.

facts.design: Aermotor LX-25 steel tower with a 7x7 metal cab

staffing.status: reported in active service; no staffing history or current staffing date found

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest, Alpine Ranger District)

events.note: Site has hosted a lookout since 1928, per NHLR
46-ft LX-25 Aermotor tower with 7x7 metal cab; Wikipedia says it was installed in 1933 and likely built by the CCC
Listed as Bear Mountain Lookout Complex, NRHP #87002452, under the multiple listing National Forest Fire Lookouts in the Southwestern Region
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register March 4, 2002

evidence.supports: Lookout on the site since 1928, in the back country of the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest
evidence.quote: In the back country of the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest lies 8538' Bear Mountain, the site of a lookout since 1928.

evidence.supports: 46-ft LX-25 Aermotor tower with 7x7 metal cab, built 1933, in active service
evidence.quote: The 46' LX-25 Aermotor tower with 7’x7' metal cab was built in 1933 and is in active service.

evidence.supports: Administered by the U.S. Forest Service
Steel Aermotor Model LX-25 tower with a 7x7 cab, constructed 1933 (West Lookouts height 45 ft 9 in)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Heights differ: NHLR gives a 46-ft tower, West Lookouts 45 ft 9 in, and Wikipedia 49 ft 9 in. The record uses NHLR's 46 ft (14.0 m), which matches Wikipedia's infobox tower height; the story reports the spread.

sources.title: Bear Mountain Lookout Complex
sources.publisher: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

notes_for_editor: Height conflicts across three sources; the story reports them. Current use rests on an undated NHLR line ('in active service'). No staffing history, access or rental source was found, so no access level is set. Living New Deal (cited by Wikipedia) appeared only as a search snippet naming a different model (MC-E4), which was not read in full and is not used. The NRHP PDF scan was unreadable.
